column1: # cliches.tsv — the single auditable home for the Botese (AI-slop cliché) phrase
# list the thesaurus seat-gate greps and the deslopper role rewrites.
# FORMAT: four TAB-separated columns, one cliché per row. Lines beginning with
# '#' and blank lines are ignored.
#   category    a coarse grouping of the cliché kind (filler-emphasis,
#               overwrought-metaphor, ...).
#   phrase      the literal, whole PHRASE to detect — usually MULTI-WORD, matched
#               case-insensitively as a unit with non-word boundaries at both ends.
#               NEVER a bare common word and NEVER a suffix pattern or heuristic
#               (the same "comprehensive list, not patterns" discipline as
#               divergences.tsv, PR #75). Multi-word so precision comes from the
#               distinctive CONSTRUCTION, not the shared word.
#   suggestion  what to write instead — prose guidance the thesaurus seat cites and
#               the deslopper applies. There is no 1:1 mechanical swap (unlike a
#               British->American spelling), so this is a rewrite direction, and the
#               matched phrase is REMOVED/REPHRASED, not substituted token-for-token.
#   notes       false-friend cautions, the legitimate literal sense, provenance.
# WHY PHRASES, NOT WORDS (precision over recall — the load-bearing decision here).
# "seam" and "load-bearing" are ordinary words with genuine literal uses: a real
# architectural seam, a Michael-Feathers testing "seam", a real load-bearing wall.
# Bare-word matching would fire on all of those. So the list enumerates the
# DISTINCTIVE cliché COLLOCATION ("load-bearing invariant", "seam where"), which the
# literal senses do not share. A false positive that rewrites a legitimate sentence
# is worse than a missed cliché — the grep can only ever match a curated phrase, and
# the thesaurus SEAT still adjudicates every hit (identifier / quote / genuine
# literal use are accepted with rationale, exactly as the orthographer seat does).
# CURATION: maintainer-reviewed on each extension (mirrors divergences.tsv). A
# gardener proposes a new phrase through a thesaurus [proposed-rule] finding; a human
# vets it before it lands. Keep phrases SPECIFIC (a construction, not a word) and add
# inflected collocations as their own rows (matching is whole-phrase, so
# "load-bearing invariant" does NOT also catch "load-bearing invariants").
# SEED: exactly the two examples the maintainer named (kriskowal, endojs/
# endo-but-for-bots#1281 review r4028527867, 2026-09-16) — "seam" and "load-bearing"
# — each enumerated as its distinctive AI-cliché collocations. Deliberately small:
# the mechanism plus these two concepts is the deliverable, not an exhaustive
# thesaurus. The list grows by maintainer-reviewed curation.
